properties.title: Regulation (EU) 2016/679 on the protection of natural persons with regard to the processing of personal data and on the free movement of such data (General Data Protection Regulation)

properties.name: Controller
properties.description: The natural or legal person, public authority, agency or other body which, alone or jointly with others, determines the purposes and means of the processing of personal data.

properties.name: Processor
properties.description: A natural or legal person, public authority, agency or other body which processes personal data on behalf of the controller.

properties.name: Joint controller
properties.description: One of two or more controllers who jointly determine the purposes and means of processing and who must transparently determine their respective responsibilities for compliance by arrangement between them.

properties.name: Representative
properties.description: A natural or legal person established in the Union who, designated by the controller or processor in writing pursuant to Article 27, represents the controller or processor with regard to their respective obligations under this Regulation.

properties.name: Data Protection Officer
properties.description: The person designated by a controller or processor, on the basis of professional qualities and expert knowledge of data protection law and practice, to inform, advise and monitor compliance and act as a contact point for the supervisory authority.

properties.name: Data Minimisation
properties.description: Capacity to limit data processing to what is adequate, relevant and necessary for the product's intended purpose.

properties.name: Access Control & Authentication
properties.description: Capacity to prevent unauthorised access via authentication and identity/access management, and to report on unauthorised access attempts.

properties.name: Data Encryption
properties.description: Capacity to protect the confidentiality of stored, transmitted or processed data using state-of-the-art encryption.

properties.name: Data & Configuration Integrity Protection
properties.description: Capacity to protect data, commands, programs and configuration against unauthorised manipulation, and to report corruption.

properties.name: Availability & Resilience
properties.description: Capacity to protect the availability of essential and basic functions, including resilience against denial-of-service attacks.

properties.name: Cybersecurity Risk Management Program
properties.description: Capacity to establish and run a program of appropriate and proportionate technical, operational and organisational measures to manage cybersecurity risk to network and information systems.

properties.name: Business Continuity & Disaster Recovery
properties.description: Capacity to maintain backup management, disaster recovery and crisis management processes that sustain operations through an incident.

properties.name: Security Control Effectiveness Assessment
properties.description: Capacity to apply policies and procedures that assess the effectiveness of an entity's cybersecurity risk-management measures.

properties.name: Asset & Personnel Security Management
properties.description: Capacity to manage human resources security and maintain an inventory and control regime over organisational assets.

properties.name: Security Incident Reporting
properties.description: Capacity to detect, assess and report actively exploited vulnerabilities and severe security incidents to competent authorities within mandated timeframes.

properties.name: Incident Handling
properties.description: Capacity to detect, respond to and contain cybersecurity incidents affecting network and information systems.

properties.name: Vulnerability Reporting & User Communication
properties.description: Capacity to operate a reachable point of contact for vulnerability reports and to communicate security-relevant information to users and third parties.

properties.name: Regulatory Cooperation
properties.description: Capacity to respond to reasoned requests from market surveillance authorities and cooperate on risk-elimination measures.

properties.name: Compliance Documentation Management
properties.description: Capacity to create, retain and make available technical documentation and declarations of conformity to market surveillance authorities.

properties.name: Secure Data Removal & Portability
properties.description: Capacity to let users securely and permanently remove product data and settings, and to transfer data to other products or systems securely.

properties.name: Lawfulness, Fairness & Transparency of Processing
properties.description: Capacity to process personal data on a lawful basis, fairly and in a transparent manner in relation to the data subject.

properties.name: Purpose Limitation Management
properties.description: Capacity to collect personal data only for specified, explicit and legitimate purposes and to assess compatibility before further processing for a new purpose.

properties.name: Data Accuracy Management
properties.description: Capacity to keep personal data accurate and up to date, and to erase or rectify inaccurate data without delay.

properties.name: Storage Limitation Management
properties.description: Capacity to keep personal data in identifiable form for no longer than necessary for the purposes of processing.

properties.name: Data Integrity & Confidentiality Assurance
properties.description: Capacity to process personal data in a manner that ensures appropriate security, including protection against unauthorised or unlawful processing and accidental loss, destruction or damage.

properties.name: Data Protection Compliance Program
properties.description: Capacity to implement, review and demonstrate risk-based technical and organisational measures and policies that ensure and evidence overall compliance with data protection law.

properties.name: Lawful Basis Determination & Documentation
properties.description: Capacity to identify and document a valid legal basis for each processing operation before it begins.

properties.name: Consent Management
properties.description: Capacity to obtain, present, record, demonstrate and enable withdrawal of data subject consent.

properties.name: Child Consent Verification
properties.description: Capacity to verify age and, where required, obtain or verify authorisation from the holder of parental responsibility before processing a child's data.

properties.name: Sensitive Data Processing Controls
properties.description: Capacity to gate processing of special-category and criminal-conviction/offence data behind a verified exception or official authorisation.

properties.name: Data Subject Rights Fulfilment & Communication
properties.description: Capacity to provide data subjects and other recipients with required information, notices and responses concerning processing and the exercise of data subject rights, within mandated timeframes and in accessible form.

properties.name: Data Subject Rights Execution
properties.description: Capacity to carry out the substantive actions that fulfil a data subject's rights: rectification, erasure, restriction, portability and cessation of processing on objection.

properties.name: Automated Decision-Making Safeguards
properties.description: Capacity to identify solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effect and apply the safeguards, exceptions and human-intervention mechanisms this requires.

properties.name: Data Protection Impact Assessment
properties.description: Capacity to assess, document and keep current the impact of high-risk processing operations on the protection of personal data.

properties.name: Regulatory Prior Consultation
properties.description: Capacity to proactively seek supervisory authority input before undertaking processing that a data protection impact assessment indicates is high-risk.

properties.name: Data Protection Officer Management
properties.description: Capacity to designate, position, resource and support a data protection officer in accordance with statutory requirements.

properties.name: Professional Secrecy & Confidentiality
properties.description: Capacity to bind personnel and role-holders to statutory or contractual secrecy and confidentiality obligations concerning personal data.

properties.name: Data Protection Advisory & Awareness
properties.description: Capacity to advise controllers, processors and staff on data protection obligations and exercise risk-based judgement in doing so.

properties.name: Data Protection Compliance Monitoring
properties.description: Capacity to monitor ongoing compliance with data protection law and internal policy, including audits, training and awareness-raising.

properties.name: Data Protection by Design & Default
properties.description: Capacity to build technical and organisational measures implementing data-protection principles into processing systems from the point of design and by default.

properties.name: Joint Controller Arrangement Management
properties.description: Capacity to establish, document and make available an arrangement determining joint controllers' respective data protection responsibilities.

properties.name: Representative Designation & Management
properties.description: Capacity to designate and maintain an EU representative addressable by supervisory authorities and data subjects on processing matters.

properties.name: Processor Due Diligence & Selection
properties.description: Capacity to assess and select processors offering sufficient guarantees to implement appropriate technical and organisational measures.

properties.name: Sub-Processor Authorisation Management
properties.description: Capacity to control the engagement of sub-processors through controller authorisation and to flow down equivalent data protection obligations.

properties.name: Processor Contract Management
properties.description: Capacity to establish, maintain and act in accordance with a binding contract or legal act governing processing carried out on behalf of a controller.

properties.name: International Data Transfer Governance
properties.description: Capacity to identify, gate and document the legal mechanism relied on for each transfer of personal data to a third country or international organisation.

properties.name: Binding Corporate Rules Governance
properties.description: Capacity to draft, maintain and enforce binding corporate rules meeting statutory content and enforceability requirements as a mechanism for intra-group international transfers.

properties.text: Personal data shall be processed lawfully, fairly and in a transparent manner in relation to the data subject ('lawfulness, fairness and transparency').
Ensure Lawfulness, Fairness and Transparency of Processing as Controller
Personal data shall be collected for specified, explicit and legitimate purposes and not further processed in a manner incompatible with those purposes.
Limit Processing to Specified, Explicit and Legitimate Purposes as Controller
Personal data shall be adequate, relevant and limited to what is necessary in relation to the purposes for which they are processed ('data minimisation').
Minimise Personal Data Processed to What Is Necessary as Controller
Personal data shall be accurate and, where necessary, kept up to date; every reasonable step must be taken to ensure that inaccurate personal data are erased or rectified without delay ('accuracy').
Ensure Personal Data Accuracy and Timely Rectification as Controller
Personal data shall be kept in a form which permits identification of data subjects for no longer than is necessary for the purposes for which they are processed ('storage limitation').
Limit Storage Duration of Identifiable Personal Data as Controller

Personal data shall be processed in a manner that ensures appropriate security of the personal data, including protection against unauthorised or unlawful processing and against accidental loss, destruction or damage, using appropriate technical or organisational measures ('integrity and confidentiality').
Ensure Integrity and Confidentiality of Personal Data as Controller
The controller shall be responsible for, and be able to demonstrate compliance with, the principles set out in paragraph 1 ('accountability').
Demonstrate Accountability for Compliance with Data Processing Principles as Controller

nodes.label: Requirement

properties.text: Processing shall be lawful only if and to the extent that at least one of the following applies: (a) consent; (b) contract performance or pre-contractual steps; (c) compliance with a legal obligation; (d) protection of vital interests; (e) performance of a task in the public interest or exercise of official authority; (f) legitimate interests, except where overridden by the data subject's interests or fundamental rights and freedoms, in particular where the data subject is a child.

nodes._comment: The six lettered grounds in Art. 6(1)(a)-(f) are alternative (disjunctive) legal bases, not cumulative duties, so they are kept as elaboration within a single Requirement rather than split, the same treatment given to Art. 46(2)'s alternative safeguard mechanisms and Art. 49(1)'s alternative derogation grounds.

properties.text: Ensure a Valid Lawful Basis for Every Processing Operation as Controller

Where processing for a purpose other than that for which the data were collected is not based on consent or on Union/Member State law, the controller shall, to ascertain compatibility, take into account: (a) any link between the purposes; (b) the context of collection; (c) the nature of the data, including special categories; (d) the possible consequences for data subjects; (e) the existence of appropriate safeguards.
Assess Compatibility Before Further Processing for a New Purpose as Controller
Where processing is based on consent, the controller shall be able to demonstrate that the data subject has consented to processing of his or her personal data.
Demonstrate Data Subject's Consent as Controller

Where consent is given in the context of a written declaration which also concerns other matters, the request for consent shall be presented in a manner clearly distinguishable from the other matters, in an intelligible and easily accessible form, using clear and plain language; any infringing part of such a declaration shall not be binding.
Present Consent Requests in Clear, Distinguishable and Plain Form as Controller

The data subject shall have the right to withdraw consent at any time, without affecting the lawfulness of processing before withdrawal; the data subject shall be informed of this prior to giving consent; it shall be as easy to withdraw as to give consent.
Enable and Facilitate Withdrawal of Consent as Easily as It Was Given as Controller

Where point (a) of Article 6(1) applies to the offer of information society services directly to a child, processing of the child's data shall be lawful where the child is at least 16 years old; where the child is below that age (which Member States may lower to no less than 13), processing shall be lawful only if consent is given or authorised by the holder of parental responsibility.
Ensure Lawful Basis for a Child's Consent to Information Society Services as Controller

The controller shall make reasonable efforts to verify in such cases that consent is given or authorised by the holder of parental responsibility over the child, taking into consideration available technology.
Verify Parental Responsibility Holder's Consent or Authorisation as Controller

nodes.label: Requirement

properties.text: Processing of special categories of personal data (revealing racial/ethnic origin, political opinions, religious/philosophical beliefs, trade union membership, genetic data, biometric data for unique identification, health data, or data concerning sex life/sexual orientation) is prohibited unless one of the exceptions in Article 9(2)(a)-(j) applies, and, for the health-data exception in point (h), only where processed by or under the responsibility of a professional subject to an obligation of secrecy.

nodes._comment: Art. 9(2)'s ten lettered exceptions are alternative (disjunctive) grounds lifting the Art. 9(1) prohibition, not stacked duties, so kept as elaboration within one Requirement. Art. 9(3)'s professional-secrecy condition on the point (h) exception is folded in as elaboration of the same exception rather than split out. Art. 9(4) (Member States may add further conditions) is excluded as a Member State legislative option, not a direct entity duty.

properties.text: Prohibit Special Category Data Processing Absent a Verified Article 9(2) Exception as Controller

Processing of personal data relating to criminal convictions and offences or related security measures based on Article 6(1) shall be carried out only under the control of official authority or when authorised by Union or Member State law providing appropriate safeguards; any comprehensive register of criminal convictions shall be kept only under the control of official authority.
Restrict Criminal Conviction and Offence Data Processing to Official Authority or Legal Authorisation as Controller

nodes.label: Requirement

properties.text: Where the controller is able to demonstrate that it is not in a position to identify the data subject, the controller shall inform the data subject accordingly, if possible; in such cases Articles 15 to 20 shall not apply except where the data subject provides additional identifying information.

nodes._comment: Art. 11(1) (relief from having to acquire identifying information solely to comply with the Regulation) is excluded as a relief from a duty, not itself a duty.

properties.text: Inform Data Subject Where Identification Is Not Possible as Controller

The controller shall take appropriate measures to provide any information referred to in Articles 13 and 14 and any communication under Articles 15 to 22 and 34 in a concise, transparent, intelligible and easily accessible form, using clear and plain language, in writing or, where appropriate, by electronic or (on request) oral means.
Provide Transparent Information and Communications in Accessible Form as Controller

The controller shall facilitate the exercise of data subject rights under Articles 15 to 22 and, save where it cannot identify the data subject, shall not refuse to act on a request for exercising those rights.
Facilitate the Exercise of Data Subject Rights as Controller

The controller shall provide information on action taken on a request under Articles 15 to 22 without undue delay and within one month of receipt (extendable by two further months for complex or numerous requests, with reasons for the delay communicated within the first month).
Respond to Data Subject Rights Requests Within One Month as Controller

If the controller does not take action on the request, it shall inform the data subject without delay and at the latest within one month of the reasons for not acting and of the possibility of lodging a complaint with a supervisory authority and seeking a judicial remedy.
Inform Data Subject of Reasons for Not Acting on a Rights Request as Controller

Information, communications and actions under Articles 13, 14 and 15 to 22 and 34 shall be provided free of charge; for manifestly unfounded or excessive requests the controller may charge a reasonable fee or refuse to act, bearing the burden of demonstrating the unfounded or excessive character of the request.
Provide Information Free of Charge Absent a Manifestly Unfounded or Excessive Request as Controller

Where personal data are collected from the data subject, the controller shall, at the time of collection, provide the data subject with the identity and contact details of the controller and, where applicable, its representative.
Disclose the identity and contact details of the controller and, where applicable, its representative at Time of Collection as Controller

Where personal data are collected from the data subject, the controller shall, at the time of collection, provide the data subject with the contact details of the data protection officer, where applicable.
Disclose the contact details of the data protection officer, where applicable at Time of Collection as Controller
Where personal data are collected from the data subject, the controller shall, at the time of collection, provide the data subject with the purposes and legal basis of the processing.
Disclose the purposes and legal basis of the processing at Time of Collection as Controller

Where personal data are collected from the data subject, the controller shall, at the time of collection, provide the data subject with where processing is based on legitimate interests, the legitimate interests pursued.
Disclose where processing is based on legitimate interests, the legitimate interests pursued at Time of Collection as Controller

Where personal data are collected from the data subject, the controller shall, at the time of collection, provide the data subject with the recipients or categories of recipients of the personal data, if any.
Disclose the recipients or categories of recipients of the personal data, if any at Time of Collection as Controller

Where personal data are collected from the data subject, the controller shall, at the time of collection, provide the data subject with where applicable, the intention to transfer personal data to a third country or international organisation and the safeguards relied on.
Disclose where applicable, the intention to transfer personal data to a third country or international organisation and the safeguards relied on at Time of Collection as Controller

In addition to Article 13(1), the controller shall, at the time of collection, provide the data subject with the period for which the data will be stored, or the criteria to determine that period, as necessary to ensure fair and transparent processing.
Disclose the period for which the data will be stored, or the criteria to determine that period to Ensure Fair and Transparent Processing as Controller

In addition to Article 13(1), the controller shall, at the time of collection, provide the data subject with the existence of the rights to access, rectification, erasure, restriction, objection and data portability, as necessary to ensure fair and transparent processing.
Disclose the existence of the rights to access, rectification, erasure, restriction, objection and data portability to Ensure Fair and Transparent Processing as Controller

In addition to Article 13(1), the controller shall, at the time of collection, provide the data subject with where processing is based on consent, the existence of the right to withdraw it at any time, as necessary to ensure fair and transparent processing.
Disclose where processing is based on consent, the existence of the right to withdraw it at any time to Ensure Fair and Transparent Processing as Controller

In addition to Article 13(1), the controller shall, at the time of collection, provide the data subject with the right to lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority, as necessary to ensure fair and transparent processing.
Disclose the right to lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority to Ensure Fair and Transparent Processing as Controller

In addition to Article 13(1), the controller shall, at the time of collection, provide the data subject with whether providing the data is a statutory or contractual requirement and the consequences of failing to provide it, as necessary to ensure fair and transparent processing.
Disclose whether providing the data is a statutory or contractual requirement and the consequences of failing to provide it to Ensure Fair and Transparent Processing as Controller

In addition to Article 13(1), the controller shall, at the time of collection, provide the data subject with the existence of automated decision-making, including profiling, and meaningful information about the logic, significance and envisaged consequences involved, as necessary to ensure fair and transparent processing.

Disclose the existence of automated decision-making, including profiling, and meaningful information about the logic, significance and envisaged consequences involved to Ensure Fair and Transparent Processing as Controller

nodes.label: Requirement

properties.text: Where the controller intends to further process the data for a purpose other than that for which they were collected, it shall provide the data subject, prior to that further processing, with information on that other purpose and any other relevant information referred to in Article 13(2).

nodes._comment: Art. 13(4) (Article 13 does not apply where the data subject already has the information) is excluded as an exemption, not a duty.

properties.text: Notify Data Subject Before Further Processing for a New Purpose as Controller

Where personal data have not been obtained from the data subject, the controller shall provide the data subject with the identity and contact details of the controller and, where applicable, its representative.
Disclose the identity and contact details of the controller and, where applicable, its representative for Data Not Obtained From the Data Subject as Controller
Where personal data have not been obtained from the data subject, the controller shall provide the data subject with the contact details of the data protection officer, where applicable.
Disclose the contact details of the data protection officer, where applicable for Data Not Obtained From the Data Subject as Controller
Where personal data have not been obtained from the data subject, the controller shall provide the data subject with the purposes and legal basis of the processing.
Disclose the purposes and legal basis of the processing for Data Not Obtained From the Data Subject as Controller
Where personal data have not been obtained from the data subject, the controller shall provide the data subject with the categories of personal data concerned.
Disclose the categories of personal data concerned for Data Not Obtained From the Data Subject as Controller
Where personal data have not been obtained from the data subject, the controller shall provide the data subject with the recipients or categories of recipients of the personal data, if any.
Disclose the recipients or categories of recipients of the personal data, if any for Data Not Obtained From the Data Subject as Controller

Where personal data have not been obtained from the data subject, the controller shall provide the data subject with where applicable, the intention to transfer personal data to a third country or international organisation and the safeguards relied on.

Disclose where applicable, the intention to transfer personal data to a third country or international organisation and the safeguards relied on for Data Not Obtained From the Data Subject as Controller

In addition to Article 14(1), the controller shall provide the data subject with the period for which the data will be stored, or the criteria to determine that period, as necessary to ensure fair and transparent processing.

In addition to Article 14(1), the controller shall provide the data subject with where processing is based on legitimate interests, the legitimate interests pursued, as necessary to ensure fair and transparent processing.
Disclose where processing is based on legitimate interests, the legitimate interests pursued to Ensure Fair and Transparent Processing as Controller

In addition to Article 14(1), the controller shall provide the data subject with the existence of the rights to access, rectification, erasure, restriction, objection and data portability, as necessary to ensure fair and transparent processing.

In addition to Article 14(1), the controller shall provide the data subject with where processing is based on consent, the existence of the right to withdraw it at any time, as necessary to ensure fair and transparent processing.
In addition to Article 14(1), the controller shall provide the data subject with the right to lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority, as necessary to ensure fair and transparent processing.

In addition to Article 14(1), the controller shall provide the data subject with the source from which the personal data originate, and whether it came from publicly accessible sources, as necessary to ensure fair and transparent processing.
Disclose the source from which the personal data originate, and whether it came from publicly accessible sources to Ensure Fair and Transparent Processing as Controller

In addition to Article 14(1), the controller shall provide the data subject with the existence of automated decision-making, including profiling, and meaningful information about the logic, significance and envisaged consequences involved, as necessary to ensure fair and transparent processing.

nodes.label: Requirement

properties.text: The controller shall provide the information referred to in Article 14(1) and (2) within a reasonable period after obtaining the data (at the latest within one month); or, if used for communication with the data subject, at the latest at the time of first communication; or, if disclosure to another recipient is envisaged, at the latest when first disclosed.

nodes._comment: Art. 14(3)(a)-(c) are alternative deadlines depending on which processing scenario applies, not cumulative duties, so kept as one Requirement.

properties.text: Provide Article 14 Information Within the Applicable Scenario-Based Deadline as Controller

nodes.label: Requirement

properties.text: Where the controller intends to further process the data for a purpose other than that for which they were obtained, it shall provide the data subject, prior to that further processing, with information on that other purpose and any other relevant information referred to in Article 14(2).

nodes._comment: Art. 14(5) (exemptions: information already held, impossible or disproportionate effort, law expressly provides for obtaining/disclosure, professional secrecy) is excluded as an exemption, not a duty.

properties.text: Notify Data Subject Before Further Processing Data Not Obtained From Them as Controller
The data subject shall have the right to obtain from the controller confirmation of whether personal data are being processed and, where so, access to the purposes of the processing.
Disclose the purposes of the processing on Access Request as Controller
The data subject shall have the right to obtain from the controller confirmation of whether personal data are being processed and, where so, access to the categories of personal data concerned.
Disclose the categories of personal data concerned on Access Request as Controller

The data subject shall have the right to obtain from the controller confirmation of whether personal data are being processed and, where so, access to the recipients or categories of recipient, in particular in third countries or international organisations.
Disclose the recipients or categories of recipient, in particular in third countries or international organisations on Access Request as Controller

The data subject shall have the right to obtain from the controller confirmation of whether personal data are being processed and, where so, access to where possible, the envisaged storage period or the criteria to determine it.
Disclose where possible, the envisaged storage period or the criteria to determine it on Access Request as Controller

The data subject shall have the right to obtain from the controller confirmation of whether personal data are being processed and, where so, access to the existence of the rights to rectification, erasure, restriction and objection.
Disclose the existence of the rights to rectification, erasure, restriction and objection on Access Request as Controller

The data subject shall have the right to obtain from the controller confirmation of whether personal data are being processed and, where so, access to the right to lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority.
Disclose the right to lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority on Access Request as Controller

The data subject shall have the right to obtain from the controller confirmation of whether personal data are being processed and, where so, access to where the data were not collected from the data subject, any available information as to their source.
Disclose where the data were not collected from the data subject, any available information as to their source on Access Request as Controller

The data subject shall have the right to obtain from the controller confirmation of whether personal data are being processed and, where so, access to the existence of automated decision-making, including profiling, and meaningful information about the logic, significance and envisaged consequences involved.
Disclose the existence of automated decision-making, including profiling, and meaningful information about the logic, significance and envisaged consequences involved on Access Request as Controller
Where personal data are transferred to a third country or international organisation, the data subject shall have the right to be informed of the appropriate safeguards relating to the transfer.
Inform Data Subject of Transfer Safeguards on Access Request as Controller

nodes.label: Requirement

properties.text: The controller shall provide a copy of the personal data undergoing processing; a reasonable fee based on administrative costs may be charged for further copies; where requested electronically, the copy shall be provided in a commonly used electronic form.

nodes._comment: Art. 15(4) (the right to obtain a copy shall not adversely affect the rights and freedoms of others) is folded in as a scope qualifier on the Art. 15(3) duty rather than extracted separately.

properties.text: Provide a Copy of Personal Data Undergoing Processing as Controller

The data subject shall have the right to obtain from the controller, without undue delay, rectification of inaccurate personal data and completion of incomplete personal data, including by means of a supplementary statement.
Rectify Inaccurate and Complete Incomplete Personal Data Without Undue Delay as Controller

nodes.label: Requirement

properties.text: The controller shall erase personal data without undue delay where one of the following grounds applies: (a) the data are no longer necessary for the purposes collected; (b) consent is withdrawn and there is no other legal ground; (c) the data subject objects and there are no overriding legitimate grounds; (d) the data have been unlawfully processed; (e) erasure is required for compliance with a legal obligation; (f) the data were collected in relation to a child's consent to information society services.

nodes._comment: Art. 17(1)(a)-(f) are alternative (disjunctive) erasure-triggering grounds, kept as elaboration within one Requirement rather than split.

properties.text: Erase Personal Data Without Undue Delay Where an Erasure Ground Applies as Controller

nodes.label: Requirement

properties.text: Where the controller has made the personal data public and is obliged to erase them, it shall take reasonable steps, including technical measures, to inform other controllers processing the data that the data subject has requested erasure of any links to, or copy or replication of, that data.

nodes._comment: Art. 17(3)(a)-(e) (exemptions: freedom of expression, legal obligation/public task, public-health public interest, archiving/research/statistics, legal claims) is excluded as an exemption, not a duty.

properties.text: Inform Other Controllers of Erasure Requests for Publicly Disclosed Data as Controller

nodes.label: Requirement

properties.text: The data subject shall have the right to obtain from the controller restriction of processing where: (a) accuracy is contested, for a period enabling verification; (b) processing is unlawful and the data subject opposes erasure, requesting restriction instead; (c) the controller no longer needs the data but the data subject needs them for legal claims; (d) the data subject has objected pending verification of overriding grounds.

nodes._comment: Art. 18(1)(a)-(d) are alternative (disjunctive) restriction-triggering grounds, kept as elaboration within one Requirement rather than split.

properties.text: Restrict Processing Where a Restriction Ground Applies as Controller

Restricted personal data shall, with the exception of storage, only be processed with the data subject's consent, for the establishment, exercise or defence of legal claims, for the protection of the rights of another person, or for reasons of important public interest.
Limit Processing of Restricted Personal Data to Permitted Grounds as Controller
A data subject who has obtained restriction of processing shall be informed by the controller before the restriction is lifted.
Inform Data Subject Before Lifting a Restriction of Processing as Controller

The controller shall communicate any rectification, erasure or restriction of processing to each recipient to whom the personal data have been disclosed, unless this proves impossible or involves disproportionate effort.
Notify Recipients of Rectification, Erasure or Restriction as Controller
The controller shall inform the data subject about those recipients if the data subject requests it.
Inform Data Subject of Recipients Notified of Rectification, Erasure or Restriction as Controller

Where processing is based on consent or on a contract and is carried out by automated means, the data subject shall have the right to receive the personal data concerning him or her in a structured, commonly used and machine-readable format and to transmit those data to another controller without hindrance.
Provide Personal Data in a Structured, Machine-Readable Format for Portability as Controller

nodes.label: Requirement

properties.text: In exercising the right to data portability, the data subject shall have the right to have the personal data transmitted directly from one controller to another, where technically feasible.

nodes._comment: Art. 20(3)-(4) (without prejudice to Art. 17; inapplicable to public-task/official-authority processing; shall not adversely affect the rights of others) are scope qualifiers, not separate duties.

properties.text: Enable Direct Controller-to-Controller Data Transmission Where Technically Feasible as Controller

Where the data subject objects, on grounds relating to their particular situation, to processing based on public interest/official authority or on legitimate interests, the controller shall no longer process the personal data unless it demonstrates compelling legitimate grounds overriding the data subject's interests, rights and freedoms, or for the establishment, exercise or defence of legal claims.
Cease Processing Upon Objection Unless Compelling Grounds Override It as Controller

nodes.label: Requirement

properties.text: Where personal data are processed for direct marketing, the data subject shall have the right to object at any time (including to related profiling), and where the data subject objects, the personal data shall no longer be processed for such purposes.

nodes._comment: Art. 21(2) (the right to object) and Art. 21(3) (the resulting duty to stop) are merged into one Requirement as a single duty told across two sentences, the same treatment CRA's methodology gave Art. 13(2)-13(3).

properties.text: Cease Direct Marketing Processing Upon Objection as Controller

nodes.label: Requirement

properties.text: At the latest at the time of first communication with the data subject, the right to object under paragraphs 1 and 2 shall be explicitly brought to the data subject's attention and presented clearly and separately from other information.

nodes._comment: Art. 21(5) (option to exercise the right to object by automated means using technical specifications) is excluded: it describes a data-subject option, not an explicit controller 'shall' duty.

properties.text: Explicitly Notify Data Subjects of the Right to Object at First Communication as Controller

Where personal data are processed for scientific, historical research or statistical purposes, the data subject shall have the right to object, on grounds relating to their particular situation, unless the processing is necessary for a public-interest task.
Honour Objection to Processing for Research or Statistical Purposes as Controller

nodes.label: Requirement

properties.text: The data subject shall have the right not to be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing, including profiling, which produces legal effects or similarly significantly affects them, unless the decision is necessary for a contract, authorised by Union/Member State law with suitable safeguards, or based on explicit consent.

nodes._comment: Art. 22(2)(a)-(c) are alternative (disjunctive) exceptions lifting the Art. 22(1) prohibition, kept as elaboration within one Requirement rather than split.

properties.text: Refrain From Solely Automated Decision-Making Absent a Permitted Exception as Controller

In the contract-necessity and explicit-consent cases, the controller shall implement suitable measures to safeguard the data subject's rights, freedoms and legitimate interests, at least the right to obtain human intervention, to express a point of view and to contest the decision.
Implement Human-Intervention Safeguards for Permitted Automated Decisions as Controller
Automated decisions shall not be based on special categories of personal data unless the explicit-consent or substantial-public-interest exception applies and suitable safeguards are in place.
Restrict Automated Decisions Based on Special Category Data as Controller

Taking into account the nature, scope, context and purposes of processing and the risks to natural persons, the controller shall implement appropriate technical and organisational measures to ensure and demonstrate that processing is performed in accordance with this Regulation, reviewing and updating those measures where necessary.
Implement and Maintain Risk-Based Compliance Measures as Controller

nodes.label: Requirement

properties.text: Where proportionate in relation to processing activities, the measures referred to in Article 24(1) shall include the implementation of appropriate data protection policies by the controller.

nodes._comment: Art. 24(3) (adherence to codes of conduct/certification may be used as an element to demonstrate compliance) is excluded as a voluntary compliance path, not a duty, the same 'may' exclusion CRA's methodology applied to Art. 13(10)-(11).

properties.text: Implement Appropriate Data Protection Policies as Controller

Taking into account the state of the art, cost, and the nature, scope, context, purposes and risks of processing, the controller shall implement appropriate technical and organisational measures, such as pseudonymisation, designed to implement data-protection principles and integrate necessary safeguards into the processing, both at the time of determining the means and at the time of processing itself.
Implement Data Protection by Design as Controller

nodes.label: Requirement

properties.text: The controller shall implement appropriate technical and organisational measures for ensuring that, by default, only personal data necessary for each specific purpose are processed, covering the amount collected, the extent of processing, the storage period and accessibility, in particular ensuring data are not made accessible without the individual's intervention to an indefinite number of persons.

nodes._comment: Art. 25(3) (certification may be used as an element to demonstrate compliance) is excluded as a voluntary compliance path.

properties.text: Implement Data Protection by Default as Controller

Where two or more controllers jointly determine the purposes and means of processing, they shall in a transparent manner determine their respective responsibilities for compliance, in particular regarding data subject rights and the duty to provide Article 13/14 information, by means of an arrangement between them (which may designate a data subject contact point), unless and to the extent their respective responsibilities are determined by Union or Member State law.
Determine Respective Responsibilities via a Transparent Arrangement as Joint controller

nodes.label: Requirement

properties.text: The arrangement shall duly reflect the respective roles and relationships of the joint controllers vis-à-vis the data subjects, and its essence shall be made available to the data subject.

nodes._comment: Art. 26(3) (irrespective of the arrangement's terms, the data subject may exercise rights against each controller) is a constraint clarifying that the arrangement cannot limit data subject rights already captured in Chapter III; it is folded in as elaboration rather than extracted as a separate duty.

properties.text: Make the Essence of the Joint Controller Arrangement Available to Data Subjects as Joint controller

nodes.label: Requirement

properties.text: Where Article 3(2) applies (processing subject to the Regulation without an EU establishment), the controller or the processor shall designate in writing a representative in the Union.

nodes._comment: Art. 27(2)(a)-(b) (exemptions for occasional, low-risk, non-large-scale processing, and for public authorities) are excluded as exemptions, not duties. Art. 27(3)'s locational criterion for where the representative must be established is folded in as elaboration of the same designation duty. Art. 27(5) (designation without prejudice to legal actions against the controller/processor themselves) is a liability-scoping clause, not a duty.

properties.text: Designate a Representative in the Union as Controller
Designate a Representative in the Union as Processor

The representative shall be mandated by the controller or processor to be addressed in addition to or instead of the controller or processor by supervisory authorities and data subjects, on all issues related to processing, for the purposes of ensuring compliance with this Regulation.
Be Addressable by Supervisory Authorities and Data Subjects on All Processing Issues as Representative

Where processing is carried out on behalf of a controller, the controller shall use only processors providing sufficient guarantees to implement appropriate technical and organisational measures meeting the Regulation's requirements and ensuring the protection of the data subject's rights.
Engage Only Processors Providing Sufficient Guarantees as Controller

The processor shall not engage another processor without prior specific or general written authorisation of the controller; under a general authorisation, the processor shall inform the controller of intended changes concerning other processors, giving the controller an opportunity to object.
Obtain Controller Authorisation Before Engaging a Sub-Processor as Processor

Processing by a processor shall be governed by a contract or other legal act under Union or Member State law, binding on the processor with regard to the controller, setting out the subject-matter, duration, nature and purpose of the processing, the type of personal data and categories of data subjects, and the obligations and rights of the controller.
Establish a Processor Contract with Required Baseline Content as Controller
Establish a Processor Contract with Required Baseline Content as Processor

The contract shall stipulate that the processor processes personal data only on documented instructions from the controller, including regarding third-country/international-organisation transfers, unless required to do otherwise by Union or Member State law (in which case it shall inform the controller of that legal requirement unless prohibited on public-interest grounds).
Process Personal Data Only on Documented Controller Instructions as Processor

The contract shall stipulate that the processor ensures persons authorised to process personal data have committed to confidentiality or are under an appropriate statutory obligation of confidentiality.
Bind Authorised Personnel to Confidentiality as Processor
The contract shall stipulate that the processor takes all measures required pursuant to Article 32.
Take All Article 32 Security Measures as Processor
The contract shall stipulate that the processor respects the conditions in Article 28(2) and (4) for engaging another processor.
Respect Sub-Processor Engagement Conditions as Processor

The contract shall stipulate that, taking into account the nature of the processing, the processor assists the controller by appropriate technical and organisational measures, insofar as possible, for fulfilling the controller's obligation to respond to data subject rights requests under Chapter III.
Assist Controller in Fulfilling Data Subject Rights Requests as Processor

The contract shall stipulate that the processor assists the controller in ensuring compliance with the obligations under Articles 32 to 36, taking into account the nature of processing and information available to the processor.
Assist Controller in Ensuring Compliance with Articles 32-36 as Processor

The contract shall stipulate that, at the controller's choice, the processor deletes or returns all personal data after the end of the provision of services and deletes existing copies, unless Union or Member State law requires storage.
Delete or Return Personal Data at End of Service Provision as Processor

nodes.label: Requirement

properties.text: The contract shall stipulate that the processor makes available to the controller all information necessary to demonstrate compliance with Article 28 and allows for and contributes to audits, including inspections; the processor shall immediately inform the controller if, in its opinion, an instruction infringes this Regulation or other data protection provisions.

nodes._comment: The trailing sentence of Art. 28(3), first subparagraph, in fine (immediately informing the controller of an infringing instruction) is folded into point (h)'s Requirement as elaboration of the same audit/compliance-demonstration duty rather than split out.

properties.text: Demonstrate Compliance and Support Controller Audits as Processor

nodes.label: Requirement

properties.text: Where a processor engages another processor for specific processing activities, the same data protection obligations set out in the controller-processor contract shall be imposed on that other processor by contract or other legal act; where the other processor fails to fulfil its obligations, the initial processor shall remain fully liable to the controller for that performance.

nodes._comment: Art. 28(5)-(8) (codes of conduct/certification as an element of sufficient guarantees; standard contractual clauses mechanics) are excluded as voluntary/institutional mechanisms, not duties.

properties.text: Impose Equivalent Data Protection Obligations on Sub-Processors as Processor

nodes.label: Requirement

properties.text: The contract or other legal act referred to in Article 28(3) and (4) shall be in writing, including in electronic form.

nodes._comment: Art. 28(10) (a processor that infringes by determining purposes/means is deemed a controller) is a deeming/legal-consequence provision, not an affirmative duty, so excluded, the same treatment CRA's methodology gave liability-scoping clauses.

properties.text: Ensure the Processor Contract Is in Writing as Controller
Ensure the Processor Contract Is in Writing as Processor

nodes.label: Requirement

properties.text: The processor and any person acting under the authority of the controller or processor who has access to personal data shall not process that data except on instructions from the controller, unless required to do so by Union or Member State law.

nodes._comment: Reuses the Processor Contract Management capability rather than minting a near-duplicate, since this is the same underlying instruction-following duty already required by Art. 28(3)(a).

properties.text: Process Personal Data Only on Controller Instructions as Processor

Each controller shall maintain a record of processing activities under its responsibility containing the name and contact details of the controller and, where applicable, the joint controller, representative and data protection officer.
Record the name and contact details of the controller and, where applicable, the joint controller, representative and data protection officer as Controller
Each controller shall maintain a record of processing activities under its responsibility containing the purposes of the processing.
Record the purposes of the processing as Controller
Each controller shall maintain a record of processing activities under its responsibility containing a description of the categories of data subjects and of personal data.
Record a description of the categories of data subjects and of personal data as Controller
Each controller shall maintain a record of processing activities under its responsibility containing the categories of recipients, including in third countries or international organisations.
Record the categories of recipients, including in third countries or international organisations as Controller

Each controller shall maintain a record of processing activities under its responsibility containing where applicable, transfers to a third country or international organisation, including identification of that country/organisation and, for Art. 49(1) second-subparagraph transfers, documentation of suitable safeguards.

Record where applicable, transfers to a third country or international organisation, including identification of that country/organisation and, for Art. 49(1) second-subparagraph transfers, documentation of suitable safeguards as Controller
Each controller shall maintain a record of processing activities under its responsibility containing where possible, the envisaged time limits for erasure of the different categories of data.
Record where possible, the envisaged time limits for erasure of the different categories of data as Controller

Each controller shall maintain a record of processing activities under its responsibility containing where possible, a general description of the Article 32(1) technical and organisational security measures.
Record where possible, a general description of the Article 32(1) technical and organisational security measures as Controller

Each processor shall maintain a record of all categories of processing activities carried out on behalf of a controller, containing the name and contact details of the processor(s), of each controller on whose behalf it acts, and, where applicable, of the representative and data protection officer.
Record the name and contact details of the processor(s), of each controller on whose behalf it acts, and, where applicable, of the representative and data protection officer as Processor

Each processor shall maintain a record of all categories of processing activities carried out on behalf of a controller, containing the categories of processing carried out on behalf of each controller.
Record the categories of processing carried out on behalf of each controller as Processor

Each processor shall maintain a record of all categories of processing activities carried out on behalf of a controller, containing where applicable, transfers to a third country or international organisation, including identification of that country/organisation and, for Art. 49(1) second-subparagraph transfers, documentation of suitable safeguards.

Record where applicable, transfers to a third country or international organisation, including identification of that country/organisation and, for Art. 49(1) second-subparagraph transfers, documentation of suitable safeguards as Processor

Each processor shall maintain a record of all categories of processing activities carried out on behalf of a controller, containing where possible, a general description of the Article 32(1) technical and organisational security measures.
Record where possible, a general description of the Article 32(1) technical and organisational security measures as Processor
The records referred to in Article 30(1) and (2) shall be in writing, including in electronic form.
Maintain Records of Processing Activities in Writing as Controller
Maintain Records of Processing Activities in Writing as Processor

nodes.label: Requirement

properties.text: The controller or processor and, where applicable, their representative, shall make the record available to the supervisory authority on request.

nodes._comment: Art. 30(5) (the <250-employee exemption, unless risk/non-occasional/special-category processing) is excluded as a scope-limiting exemption, not a duty.

properties.text: Make Records of Processing Activities Available to Supervisory Authority on Request as Controller
Make Records of Processing Activities Available to Supervisory Authority on Request as Processor
The controller and the processor and, where applicable, their representatives, shall cooperate, on request, with the supervisory authority in the performance of its tasks.
Cooperate with Supervisory Authority on Request as Controller
Cooperate with Supervisory Authority on Request as Processor

Taking into account the state of the art, costs, and the nature, scope, context, purposes and risk of processing, the controller and the processor shall implement appropriate technical and organisational measures to ensure a level of security appropriate to the risk.
Implement Risk-Appropriate Security Measures as Controller
Implement Risk-Appropriate Security Measures as Processor
Security measures shall include, as appropriate, the pseudonymisation and encryption of personal data.
Apply Pseudonymisation and Encryption as Controller
Apply Pseudonymisation and Encryption as Processor
Security measures shall include, as appropriate, the ability to ensure the ongoing confidentiality, integrity, availability and resilience of processing systems and services.
Ensure Confidentiality, Integrity, Availability and Resilience of Processing Systems as Controller
Ensure Confidentiality, Integrity, Availability and Resilience of Processing Systems as Processor
Security measures shall include, as appropriate, the ability to restore the availability and access to personal data in a timely manner in the event of a physical or technical incident.
Restore Availability and Access to Personal Data After an Incident as Controller
Restore Availability and Access to Personal Data After an Incident as Processor

nodes.label: Requirement

properties.text: Security measures shall include, as appropriate, a process for regularly testing, assessing and evaluating the effectiveness of technical and organisational measures for ensuring security of processing.

nodes._comment: Art. 32(2) (risk factors to take into account, in particular accidental/unlawful destruction, loss, alteration, disclosure of or access to data) is folded in as elaboration of the Art. 32(1) risk assessment rather than a separate duty. Art. 32(3) (codes of conduct/certification as an element of demonstrating compliance) is excluded as a voluntary compliance path.

properties.text: Regularly Test and Evaluate Security Measure Effectiveness as Controller
Regularly Test and Evaluate Security Measure Effectiveness as Processor

The controller and processor shall take steps to ensure that any natural person acting under their authority with access to personal data does not process it except on instructions, unless required to do so by Union or Member State law.
Ensure Personnel Process Personal Data Only on Instructions as Controller
Ensure Personnel Process Personal Data Only on Instructions as Processor

In the case of a personal data breach, the controller shall, without undue delay and, where feasible, within 72 hours of becoming aware of it, notify the breach to the competent supervisory authority, unless the breach is unlikely to result in a risk to natural persons' rights and freedoms; a notification made after 72 hours shall be accompanied by reasons for the delay.
Notify Personal Data Breach to Supervisory Authority Within 72 Hours as Controller
The processor shall notify the controller without undue delay after becoming aware of a personal data breach.
Notify Controller of Personal Data Breach Without Undue Delay as Processor

The notification referred to in Article 33(1) shall at least describe the nature of the breach, including, where possible, the categories and approximate number of data subjects and personal data records concerned.
Describe the nature of the breach, including, where possible, the categories and approximate number of data subjects and personal data records concerned in Breach Notification as Controller
The notification referred to in Article 33(1) shall at least communicate the name and contact details of the data protection officer or other contact point.
Communicate the name and contact details of the data protection officer or other contact point in Breach Notification as Controller
The notification referred to in Article 33(1) shall at least describe the likely consequences of the breach.
Describe the likely consequences of the breach in Breach Notification as Controller

The notification referred to in Article 33(1) shall at least describe the measures taken or proposed to address the breach, including, where appropriate, measures to mitigate its possible adverse effects.
Describe the measures taken or proposed to address the breach, including, where appropriate, measures to mitigate its possible adverse effects in Breach Notification as Controller

nodes.label: Requirement

properties.text: The controller shall document any personal data breaches, comprising the facts, effects and remedial action taken, enabling the supervisory authority to verify compliance with Article 33.

nodes._comment: Art. 33(4) (information may be provided in phases where not all available at once) is folded in as elaboration of the Art. 33(1) notification duty rather than a separate duty.

properties.text: Document Personal Data Breaches for Supervisory Authority Verification as Controller

nodes.label: Requirement

properties.text: When a personal data breach is likely to result in a high risk to natural persons' rights and freedoms, the controller shall communicate the breach to the data subject without undue delay, describing in clear and plain language the nature of the breach and containing at least the information in Article 33(3), points (b), (c) and (d).

nodes._comment: Art. 34(2)'s content requirement is merged into 34.1 as a direct cross-reference to Art. 33(3)(b)-(d), already captured. Art. 34(3)(a)-(c) (exceptions: protective measures applied, subsequent risk-mitigating measures, disproportionate effort with public communication instead) are folded in as conditions/an alternative compliance path on the same duty rather than split out, the same treatment CRA's methodology gave Art. 13(11)'s conditional public-archive duty. Art. 34(4) (the supervisory authority may require or deem the duty satisfied) is an authority power, not an entity duty.

properties.text: Communicate High-Risk Personal Data Breach to the Data Subject as Controller

Where a type of processing, in particular using new technologies, is likely to result in a high risk to natural persons' rights and freedoms, the controller shall, prior to the processing, carry out an assessment of the impact of the envisaged processing operations on the protection of personal data; a single assessment may address a set of similar operations presenting similar high risks.
Carry Out a Data Protection Impact Assessment for High-Risk Processing as Controller

nodes.label: Requirement

properties.text: The controller shall seek the advice of the data protection officer, where designated, when carrying out a data protection impact assessment.

nodes._comment: Art. 35(3)(a)-(c)'s enumerated cases (systematic/extensive automated evaluation with legal/significant effect; large-scale special-category or criminal data processing; systematic large-scale monitoring of a public area) are folded into Art. 35(1)'s Requirement as elaboration of when the DPIA duty applies, not extracted as separate Requirements. Art. 35(4)-(6) (supervisory authority list-publishing and consistency-mechanism duties) are institutional, not controller duties.

properties.text: Seek Data Protection Officer's Advice on the DPIA as Controller

The data protection impact assessment shall contain at least a systematic description of the envisaged processing operations and purposes, including, where applicable, the legitimate interest pursued.
Include a systematic description of the envisaged processing operations and purposes, including, where applicable, the legitimate interest pursued in the DPIA as Controller
The data protection impact assessment shall contain at least an assessment of the necessity and proportionality of the processing operations in relation to the purposes.
Include an assessment of the necessity and proportionality of the processing operations in relation to the purposes in the DPIA as Controller
The data protection impact assessment shall contain at least an assessment of the risks to the rights and freedoms of data subjects.
Include an assessment of the risks to the rights and freedoms of data subjects in the DPIA as Controller

The data protection impact assessment shall contain at least the measures envisaged to address the risks, including safeguards, security measures and mechanisms to ensure protection of personal data and demonstrate compliance.
Include the measures envisaged to address the risks, including safeguards, security measures and mechanisms to ensure protection of personal data and demonstrate compliance in the DPIA as Controller

nodes.label: Requirement

properties.text: Where appropriate, the controller shall seek the views of data subjects or their representatives on the intended processing, without prejudice to the protection of commercial or public interests or the security of processing operations.

nodes._comment: Art. 35(8) (adherence to approved codes of conduct taken into account by others assessing impact) and Art. 35(10) (exemption where a general legislative impact assessment already covered the processing) are excluded as, respectively, a factor for another party's assessment and an exemption, not controller duties.

properties.text: Seek Data Subjects' Views on Intended Processing Where Appropriate as Controller

Where necessary, the controller shall carry out a review to assess if processing is performed in accordance with the data protection impact assessment, at least when there is a change in the risk represented by the processing operations.
Review the DPIA When Processing Risk Changes as Controller

The controller shall consult the supervisory authority prior to processing where a data protection impact assessment indicates that the processing would result in a high risk in the absence of mitigating measures.
Consult Supervisory Authority Prior to High-Risk Processing as Controller

When consulting the supervisory authority under Article 36(1), the controller shall provide where applicable, the respective responsibilities of the controller, joint controllers and processors involved, in particular for processing within a group of undertakings.

Provide where applicable, the respective responsibilities of the controller, joint controllers and processors involved, in particular for processing within a group of undertakings to Supervisory Authority on Consultation as Controller
When consulting the supervisory authority under Article 36(1), the controller shall provide the purposes and means of the intended processing.
Provide the purposes and means of the intended processing to Supervisory Authority on Consultation as Controller
When consulting the supervisory authority under Article 36(1), the controller shall provide the measures and safeguards provided to protect the rights and freedoms of data subjects.
Provide the measures and safeguards provided to protect the rights and freedoms of data subjects to Supervisory Authority on Consultation as Controller
When consulting the supervisory authority under Article 36(1), the controller shall provide where applicable, the contact details of the data protection officer.
Provide where applicable, the contact details of the data protection officer to Supervisory Authority on Consultation as Controller
When consulting the supervisory authority under Article 36(1), the controller shall provide the data protection impact assessment provided for in Article 35.
Provide the data protection impact assessment provided for in Article 35 to Supervisory Authority on Consultation as Controller
When consulting the supervisory authority under Article 36(1), the controller shall provide any other information requested by the supervisory authority.
Provide any other information requested by the supervisory authority to Supervisory Authority on Consultation as Controller

nodes.label: Requirement

properties.text: The controller and the processor shall designate a data protection officer in any case where: (a) processing is carried out by a public authority or body (except courts acting judicially); (b) the core activities consist of processing operations requiring regular and systematic monitoring of data subjects on a large scale; or (c) the core activities consist of large-scale processing of special-category or criminal-conviction/offence data.

nodes._comment: Art. 37(2)-(3) (group-of-undertakings and multi-public-body shared DPO options) are excluded as permissive options. Art. 37(4)'s conditional Union/Member State law duty to designate outside the Art. 37(1) cases is folded into this Requirement as the same underlying designation duty rather than split out.

properties.text: Designate a Data Protection Officer Where Required as Controller
Designate a Data Protection Officer Where Required as Processor

nodes.label: Requirement

properties.text: The data protection officer shall be designated on the basis of professional qualities and, in particular, expert knowledge of data protection law and practice and the ability to fulfil the Article 39 tasks.

nodes._comment: Art. 37(6) (the DPO may be staff or under a service contract) is excluded as a permissive option, not a duty.

properties.text: Designate DPO Based on Professional Qualities and Expert Knowledge as Controller
Designate DPO Based on Professional Qualities and Expert Knowledge as Processor
The controller or the processor shall publish the contact details of the data protection officer and communicate them to the supervisory authority.
Publish and Communicate DPO Contact Details as Controller
Publish and Communicate DPO Contact Details as Processor
The controller and the processor shall ensure that the data protection officer is involved, properly and in a timely manner, in all issues which relate to the protection of personal data.
Ensure Timely Involvement of the Data Protection Officer as Controller
Ensure Timely Involvement of the Data Protection Officer as Processor

The controller and processor shall support the data protection officer in performing the Article 39 tasks by providing the resources necessary to carry out those tasks and access to personal data and processing operations, and to maintain expert knowledge.
Support DPO with Necessary Resources and Access as Controller
Support DPO with Necessary Resources and Access as Processor

nodes.label: Requirement

properties.text: The controller and processor shall ensure the data protection officer does not receive instructions regarding the exercise of their tasks, is not dismissed or penalised for performing them, and reports directly to the highest management level.

nodes._comment: Art. 38(4) (data subjects may contact the DPO) is excluded: it describes a data-subject option enabled by the Art. 37(7) publication duty already captured, not a new controller/processor duty.

properties.text: Ensure DPO Independence and a Direct Reporting Line as Controller
Ensure DPO Independence and a Direct Reporting Line as Processor
The data protection officer shall be bound by secrecy or confidentiality concerning the performance of their tasks, in accordance with Union or Member State law.
Maintain Secrecy and Confidentiality Concerning Task Performance as Data Protection Officer
The data protection officer may fulfil other tasks and duties; the controller or processor shall ensure that any such tasks and duties do not result in a conflict of interests.
Ensure No Conflict of Interest in the DPO's Other Tasks as Controller
Ensure No Conflict of Interest in the DPO's Other Tasks as Processor

The data protection officer shall at least inform and advise the controller or processor and the employees who carry out processing of their obligations under this Regulation and other Union or Member State data protection provisions.
Inform and Advise on Data Protection Obligations as Data Protection Officer

The data protection officer shall at least monitor compliance with this Regulation, other data protection provisions and the controller's or processor's policies, including the assignment of responsibilities, awareness-raising and staff training, and related audits.
Monitor Data Protection Compliance as Data Protection Officer
The data protection officer shall at least provide advice, where requested, on the data protection impact assessment and monitor its performance pursuant to Article 35.
Advise on and Monitor Data Protection Impact Assessments as Data Protection Officer
The data protection officer shall at least cooperate with the supervisory authority.
Cooperate with Supervisory Authority as Data Protection Officer

The data protection officer shall at least act as the contact point for the supervisory authority on issues relating to processing, including the Article 36 prior consultation, and consult, where appropriate, on any other matter.
Act as Supervisory Authority Contact Point as Data Protection Officer

The data protection officer shall, in performing their tasks, have due regard to the risk associated with processing operations, taking into account the nature, scope, context and purposes of processing.
Exercise Risk-Based Judgement in Performing DPO Tasks as Data Protection Officer

Any transfer of personal data undergoing or intended for processing after transfer to a third country or international organisation shall take place only if the conditions in this Chapter are complied with by the controller and processor, including for onward transfers, so that the level of protection guaranteed by this Regulation is not undermined.
Ensure Compliance with Chapter V Conditions for International Transfers as Controller
Ensure Compliance with Chapter V Conditions for International Transfers as Processor

nodes.label: Requirement

properties.text: In the absence of an Article 45(3) adequacy decision, a controller or processor may transfer personal data to a third country or international organisation only if it has provided appropriate safeguards, and on condition that enforceable data subject rights and effective legal remedies are available.

nodes._comment: Art. 46(2)(a)-(f)'s list of safeguard mechanisms available without specific authorisation (binding legal instrument, BCRs, Commission/supervisory-authority SCCs, code of conduct, certification) are alternative (disjunctive) means of satisfying the Art. 46(1) duty, folded in as elaboration rather than split, the same treatment given Art. 6(1)'s alternative lawful bases.

properties.text: Ensure Appropriate Safeguards and Enforceable Rights Before Transfer as Controller
Ensure Appropriate Safeguards and Enforceable Rights Before Transfer as Processor

nodes.label: Requirement

properties.text: Subject to authorisation from the competent supervisory authority, appropriate safeguards may also be provided by ad hoc contractual clauses between the parties, or by provisions in administrative arrangements between public authorities including enforceable and effective data subject rights.

nodes._comment: Art. 46(4) (supervisory authority consistency-mechanism application) and Art. 46(5) (legacy Directive 95/46/EC authorisations remaining valid) are institutional/transitional, not entity duties.

properties.text: Obtain Supervisory Authority Authorisation for Ad Hoc Transfer Safeguards as Controller
Obtain Supervisory Authority Authorisation for Ad Hoc Transfer Safeguards as Processor

The competent supervisory authority shall approve binding corporate rules provided that they are legally binding on and enforced by every group member including employees, expressly confer enforceable rights on data subjects, and fulfil the Article 47(2) content requirements.
Ensure Binding Corporate Rules Are Legally Binding and Confer Enforceable Data Subject Rights as Controller
Ensure Binding Corporate Rules Are Legally Binding and Confer Enforceable Data Subject Rights as Processor
The binding corporate rules referred to in Article 47(1) shall specify at least the structure and contact details of the group and each of its members.
Specify the structure and contact details of the group and each of its members in Binding Corporate Rules as Controller
Specify the structure and contact details of the group and each of its members in Binding Corporate Rules as Processor

The binding corporate rules referred to in Article 47(1) shall specify at least the data transfers or set of transfers, including categories of personal data, type and purpose of processing, type of data subjects affected and the third countries in question.

Specify the data transfers or set of transfers, including categories of personal data, type and purpose of processing, type of data subjects affected and the third countries in question in Binding Corporate Rules as Controller

Specify the data transfers or set of transfers, including categories of personal data, type and purpose of processing, type of data subjects affected and the third countries in question in Binding Corporate Rules as Processor
The binding corporate rules referred to in Article 47(1) shall specify at least their legally binding nature, both internally and externally.
Specify their legally binding nature, both internally and externally in Binding Corporate Rules as Controller
Specify their legally binding nature, both internally and externally in Binding Corporate Rules as Processor

The binding corporate rules referred to in Article 47(1) shall specify at least the application of the general data protection principles, including purpose limitation, data minimisation, storage limitation, data quality, data protection by design and by default, legal basis, special-category processing, security measures and onward-transfer requirements.

Specify the application of the general data protection principles, including purpose limitation, data minimisation, storage limitation, data quality, data protection by design and by default, legal basis, special-category processing, security measures and onward-transfer requirements in Binding Corporate Rules as Controller

Specify the application of the general data protection principles, including purpose limitation, data minimisation, storage limitation, data quality, data protection by design and by default, legal basis, special-category processing, security measures and onward-transfer requirements in Binding Corporate Rules as Processor
