The binding corporate rules referred to in Article 47(1) shall specify at least the rights of data subjects regarding processing and the means to exercise them, including the right not to be subject to solely automated decisions, the right to lodge a complaint, and the right to redress and compensation for a breach of the rules.

Specify the rights of data subjects regarding processing and the means to exercise them, including the right not to be subject to solely automated decisions, the right to lodge a complaint, and the right to redress and compensation for a breach of the rules in Binding Corporate Rules as Controller

Specify the rights of data subjects regarding processing and the means to exercise them, including the right not to be subject to solely automated decisions, the right to lodge a complaint, and the right to redress and compensation for a breach of the rules in Binding Corporate Rules as Processor

The binding corporate rules referred to in Article 47(1) shall specify at least the acceptance of liability by the EU-established controller or processor for breaches by any non-EU group member, with an exemption only if it proves that member is not responsible.

Specify the acceptance of liability by the EU-established controller or processor for breaches by any non-EU group member, with an exemption only if it proves that member is not responsible in Binding Corporate Rules as Controller

Specify the acceptance of liability by the EU-established controller or processor for breaches by any non-EU group member, with an exemption only if it proves that member is not responsible in Binding Corporate Rules as Processor

The binding corporate rules referred to in Article 47(1) shall specify at least how information on the binding corporate rules, in particular points (d), (e) and (f), is provided to data subjects in addition to Articles 13 and 14.
Specify how information on the binding corporate rules, in particular points (d), (e) and (f), is provided to data subjects in addition to Articles 13 and 14 in Binding Corporate Rules as Controller
Specify how information on the binding corporate rules, in particular points (d), (e) and (f), is provided to data subjects in addition to Articles 13 and 14 in Binding Corporate Rules as Processor

nodes.label: Requirement

properties.text: In the absence of an adequacy decision or appropriate safeguards (including binding corporate rules), a transfer or set of transfers shall take place only on one of the following conditions: (a) explicit informed consent to the proposed transfer; (b) necessity for performance of a contract between the data subject and the controller, or pre-contractual measures; (c) necessity for conclusion/performance of a contract in the data subject's interest between the controller and another person; (d) necessity for important reasons of public interest; (e) necessity for the establishment, exercise or defence of legal claims; (f) necessity to protect vital interests where the data subject is incapable of giving consent; (g) transfer from a public register open to consultation, within the conditions for consultation laid down by law.

nodes._comment: Art. 49(1)(a)-(g) are alternative (disjunctive) derogation grounds, kept as elaboration within one Requirement rather than split, the same treatment given Art. 6(1) and Art. 46(2).

properties.text: Ensure a Derogation Condition Is Met for Transfer Absent Adequacy Decision or Safeguards as Controller

Where a transfer could not be based on Article 45 or 46 (including binding corporate rules) and no derogation applies, a transfer may take place only if it is not repetitive, concerns a limited number of data subjects, is necessary for compelling legitimate interests not overridden by the data subject's interests or rights, and the controller has assessed the circumstances and provided suitable safeguards; the controller shall inform the supervisory authority of the transfer and, in addition to Articles 13 and 14, inform the data subject of the transfer and the compelling legitimate interests pursued.
Assess Fallback Transfer Conditions and Notify Authority and Data Subject as Controller

nodes.label: Requirement

properties.text: A transfer under the public-register derogation shall not involve the entirety of the personal data or entire categories of data in the register; where the register is intended for consultation by persons with a legitimate interest, the transfer shall be made only at the request of those persons or if they are to be the recipients.

nodes._comment: Art. 49(3) (the consent/contract derogations and the fallback subparagraph do not apply to public authorities exercising public powers), Art. 49(4) (the public-interest ground must be recognised in Union/Member State law) and Art. 49(5) (Member State law may set limits for important public interest reasons and shall notify the Commission) are scope-limiting/Member-State-legislative provisions, not entity duties.

properties.text: Limit Public-Register Transfers to the Necessary Scope as Controller
The controller or processor shall document the fallback assessment and the suitable safeguards referred to in Article 49(1), second subparagraph, in the Article 30 records.
